title: The common-zero independence-number conjecture for finite groups
statement: Let $G$ be a finite group. The **common-zero graph** $\Gamma_v(G)$ has the non-linear irreducible characters of $G$ as vertices, with two characters adjacent when they have a common zero, meaning that both vanish at some element of $G$. **Common-zero independence-number conjecture.** For any four non-linear irreducible characters of $G$, two have a common zero; if $G$ is solvable, then for any three non-linear irreducible characters of $G$, two have a common zero. Equivalently, the independence number of $\Gamma_v(G)$ is at most three for arbitrary groups and at most two for solvable groups. This is presented as a weaker form of the three-class vanishing conjecture and is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Mark L. Lewis, Lucia Morotti, Emanuele Pacifici, Lucia Sanus and Hung P. Tong-Viet, “On common zeros of characters of finite groups”, arXiv:2409.14811 (2024).
references:
